extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Shared Task Dataset
extraction.description: A dataset for language-independent named entity recognition covering English and German news text, annotated with four types of named entities: persons (PER), locations (LOC), organizations (ORG), and miscellaneous names (MISC).
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder
extraction.citeAs: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder. 2003. Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. In Proceedings of CoNLL-2003.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus, with training and development sets taken from stories at the end of August 1996, the test set from December 1996, and raw unannotated data from September 1996. The German data was extracted from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (specifically the newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau), with training, development, and test sets taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992, and raw unannotated data from September to December 1992.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Reuters Corpus (news stories between August 1996 and August 1997) for English; ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (articles from the Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper from 1992) for German.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two basic language-specific tokenizers were created. The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. The German data was lemmatized, tagged, and chunked by the decision tree tagger TreeTagger. Data was formatted with one word per line and empty lines representing sentence boundaries, with four fields per line: word, part-of-speech tag, chunk tag, and named entity tag.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp, mostly following MUC conventions with an extra MISC category added for miscellaneous names (such as adjectives and events). The IOB tagging scheme was applied with tags PER, ORG, LOC, and MISC, assuming named entities are non-recursive and non-overlapping, with only top-level entities annotated when embedded.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators at the University of Antwerp
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, parameter tuning (development), and testing of machine learning systems for named entity recognition.
